data.body:
Operator 2026-10-22 (verbatim): "Investigate dsh - deepseek harness (https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) and see how we could use it as an agent, how we can integrate with it, or integrate ddflow to be with, by dsh and add it to the supported list of coding agents we have"

Evidence: docs/ddflow/research/dsh.md (task DSH-research), source read at deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness commit 687f282 (v0.2.1-rc.2); nothing was executed.

VERDICT: dsh (npm @deepseek-ai/dsh, MIT, DeepSeek AI, developer preview, TypeScript on Cordis, Node >=22.19) is a real, general coding-agent harness: web UI, headless one-shot (--json), SDK JSON-RPC, and an ACP stdio server. It is NOT tied to DeepSeek models (pi-ai providers, OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic custom endpoints). It reads AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md natively, .agents/skills, a built-in MCP client (stdio and streamable HTTP, tools list_changed honoured, no elicitation or prompts), and has OPT-IN experimental bridges that run existing Claude Code and Codex hooks.json command hooks. TRAPS: MCP servers and hooks are configured only through Cordis YAML patch layers (profile, home, or --patch), never a project file; hooks bridges are not in any shipped bundle; stdio MCP children get a scrubbed env (KEY/PASSWORD/SECRET/TOKEN and all DSH_* dropped); headless approval has no answerer (ask resolves unavailable, fail closed) unless DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=danger-full-access; instruction budget 64 KiB; hook transcript_path is always empty; SessionStart hooks run detached.

ALREADY PLANNED, LINKED NOT RE-ADDED: descriptors = P-agent-parity.new-descriptors and descriptor-v2; lane launcher = P-agent-parity.launcher; ACP = P-acp (AC-*); verify/manifest = P-agent-lifecycle; profiles = MTD-profiles; client table = SU-client-table; transcript import = B-am-ingest; lean start = P-lean-start.

WAVES: see the verified line appended after the tasks were filed.

Docs only; deliberately NOT held behind the core/docs wave.

data.body: dsh registers MCP servers and hook bridges only in Cordis patch layers: $DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>/cordis.patch.yml, $DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml, or a --patch FILE overlay at launch (apps/cli/README.md, mcp-client README). No project-local file is read, so the descriptor [mcp] path/shape vocabulary (mcpServers, servers, mcp.servers, opencode, copilot, toml.mcp_servers, none) cannot say it, and shape none would be a false 'documented absent'. Add shape cordis-patch-yaml: a writer that creates/updates ONE ddflow-owned overlay file (default .ddflow/harness/dsh.cordis.yml, region-marked, digest recorded in the manifest), idempotent, uninstall restores. The entry is { id: ddflow, name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client', config: { serverName: ddflow, transport: stdio, command, args, env, cwd } } with serverName <=32 chars [A-Za-z0-9_-] so tools read mcp__ddflow__*. Never edit $DSH_HOME without consent. Same gap exists for ACP-injected servers (session/new mcpServers): note the shape name leaves room. Unattended, no operator question. Filed as the generic descriptor gap this research found.
data.title: Descriptor MCP shape for launch-time config: ddflow can write a ddflow-owned Cordis YAML overlay (insert rows for dsh-mcp-client and hooks bridge) and report it; generic for any agent whose MCP/hook config is a launch flag or ACP session/new, not a project file

data.body: Needs Node >=22.19 and consent per D-agent-compat (install a missing agent CLI into a scratch directory, per agent). In a scratch DSH_HOME, never the real one: npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --version; dsh --profile headless --dump-default-config; --dump-config-schema (read the schema-dump safety note first); a headless --json run against a fake OpenAI-compatible endpoint (our own stub, no key) to record the event stream, final event, exit codes and what happens at an approval ask with no answerer; an MCP handshake against a ddflow stdio stub recording clientInfo, protocolVersion, capabilities, tools/list_changed handling, and whether tools appear before the first turn; the hooks-claude-code bridge with a recording hook script (payloads for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, tool names, whether SessionStart context arrives before turn 1); the ACP initialize result. Output: docs/ddflow/research/dsh-probe.md and recorded fixtures under tests/fixtures/dsh_probe/. If node, network, or consent is missing the facts stay UNKNOWN and the task records unavailable; the descriptor is then written from the source-read facts with recorded:false. Mark which claims of DSH-research were confirmed, refuted.

Ask the operator (AskUserQuestion) and file docs/ddflow/decisions/dsh.md. Recommended defaults in brackets. (1) Tier: [tier 2 fixtures-only now; tier 1 live smoke only after DSH-lane proves a headless run with a stub endpoint]. (2) Where adopt writes config: [only a ddflow-owned overlay file in the repo plus a printed launch line (dsh --profile

--patch .ddflow/harness/dsh.cordis.yml); never edit $DSH_HOME profiles without per-agent consent]. (3) Hooks: [mount the opt-in experimental hooks-claude-code bridge from the overlay, fail open; claim/lease enforcement via PreToolUse only when the bridge is verified loaded, else reported unavailable]. (4) Lane permission: [lane-private DSH_HOME, workspace-write sandbox, approval resolved by the ddflow permission broker over ACP; headless lanes only with DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=danger-full-access inside a disposable worktree/container, operator opt-in]. (5) Credentials: [env only, never argv or committed; lane-private DSH_HOME so the user's stored keys are not read]. (6) Telemetry: [dsh product telemetry is Desktop-only and opt-in; record, do not toggle]. (7) Reviewer role: [no dsh reviewer; keep direct OpenAI-compatible reviewers, because ddflow review needs a diff in and a verdict out, not an agent loop]. (8) Review independence: [family is the model family of the run, not the harness: a dsh run on a DeepSeek model is family deepseek and cannot be reviewed by lan-deepseek-*]. (9) Ship ddflow as a dsh bundle package: [defer; overlay first].
